Order 
Case Diary is perused.
The applicants has filed this First application u/S 438, Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail.
Applicants apprehends their arrest in connection with Crime No.27/2024 registered at Police Station Badoda, District Sheopur for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 406, 409, 120B of IPC.

The case of the prosecution in nutshell is that some of the villagers o f village Behdavad and Kalukhedali, Tehsil Badoda, Sheopur had made written complaints against co-accused who is Sarpanch of village Behdavad, Gram Rojgar Sahayak and present applicants and on investigation on the said complaints, the applicants and co-accused were found to have misappropriated certain government funds meant for making payment to the persons who had worked under MANREGA scheme, by creating job cards of the family members and getting enriched themselves by disbursing the amount in their accounts.
After conclusion of the enquiry, proceedings under Section 40 of the MP Panchayat and Gram Swaraj Adhiniyam 1993 were initiated against the co-accused (Sarpanch) and it was found that the applicants and co- accused were liable to refund a sum of Rs.1,18,082/- which was credited to the accounts of his family members and after depositing of the said amount, the enquiry under Section 40 of MP Panchayat and Gram Swaraj Adhiniyam was closed.

sentences.text: Thereafter, the CEO Janpad Panchayat, Sheopur lodged a complaint against the applicants and co-accused with SHO P.S. Badoda, Sheopur and on the basis of the complaint an FIR was registered at Crime No.27/2024 under Sections 420, 406, 409, 120B of IPC against the applicants along with other co-accused person.

Learned counsel for the applicants has argued that already the liability of the amount fixed upon the applicants had been deposited and the enquiry against co-accused under Section 40 of the MP Panchayat and Gram Swaraj Adhiniyam had been closed, wherein as sum or Rs.1,18,182/- had already been deposited by co-accused (sarpanch).

It was further submitted that the offence under Sections 406, 420 and 409 of IPC against the present applicants is not made out as there is no criminal breach of trust on their behalf as no public fund was entrusted to them which they had defalcated.

I t was further submitted that the present applicants are family members of co-accused Hansraj Meena (Sarpanch) who has already been granted bail and at the most the act of the co-accused's can be said to be an irregularity while creating job cards of each and every family members i.e. present applicants, for which he had already been penalized.

It was further submitted that the custodial interrogation of the present applicants is not required in the matter as nothing further is to be recovered from them and, therefore, they are entitled for grant of anticipatory bail.

On the other hand, learned Government Advocate submits that there is clear allegation against the present applicants of being beneficiaries of the illegal job cards created by co-accused in their names, whereas the job card of only the head of the family could have been prepared and, thus, the present applicants along with co-accused Sarpanch and Gram Rojgar Sahayak had created false job cards in their names and had got credit of the amount in their accounts, thus, has misappropriated the funds which was entrusted to Sarpanch by the Government for the work carried out under MANREGA scheme.

It was further submitted that in the inquiry conducted under Section 40 of MP Panchayat and Gram Swaraj Adhiniyam the co-accused had been found to be a culprit and had been directed to deposit the amount.
Thus, it was prayed that the present application be rejected.

After hearing rival contentions and perusing the case diary, this Court finds that one of similarly situated co-accused Hansraj Meena had been enlarged on anticipatory bail and custodial interrogation of the present applicants is not required in the matter as already an enquiry has been conducted by the department while initiating proceedings under Section 40 of the MP Panchayat and Gram Swaraj Adhiniyam and it has been found that the present applicants had wrongly disbursed amount of Rs.1,18,082/- in their accounts which had been directed to be refunded to State Exchequer and as per the statements made by the counsel for the petitioner at bar, the said amount has already been refunded by Sarpanch.
So far as the allegations made by the State in the FIR a sum of Rs.1,73,383/- is the amount which is stated to have been defalcated by the applicants, in connivance with the co-accused persons, which though had already been deposited by co-accused, this Court deems it expedient to direct the applicants to deposit further sum of Rs. 20,000/- each in the account of Gram Panchayat,
Behdavad.

sentences.text: Thus, on the aforesaid count and after considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court allows to grant anticipatory bail.
Accordingly, the instant application is allowed and it is directed that in the event of arrest,
applicants

be released on bail on each furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
(Rupees One Lakh only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer (Investigating Officer).
The applicants shall make themselves available for interrogation by the Investigating Officer as and when required.
The applicants will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be.
A copy of this order be sent to the trial court concerned for compliance.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Thus, on the aforesaid count and after considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court allows to grant anticipatory bail.
Accordingly, the instant application is allowed and it is directed that in the event of arrest,
applicants
be released on bail on each furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
(Rupees One Lakh only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer (Investigating Officer).
The applicants shall make themselves available for interrogation by the Investigating Officer as and when required.
They shall further abide by the other conditions enumerated in sub-section (2) of Section 438 of Cr.P.C.
This order will remain operative subject to compliance of the following conditions by the applicants:-
1. The applicants will comply with all the terms and conditions of the bond executed by him;
2. The applicants will cooperate in the investigation/trial, as the case may be;
3. The applicants will not indulge himself in extending inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as t o dissuade him/her from disclosing such facts to the Court tor to the Police Officer, as the case may be;
4 . The applicants shall not commit any other offence during pendency of the trial,
failing which this bail order shall stand cancelled automatically, without further reference to the Bench;
5. The applicants will not seek unnecessary adjournments during the trial; and 6.
The applicants will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be.
A copy of this order be sent to the trial court concerned for compliance.
Certified copy as per rules.
